topIssues.title: simulate-stack is RPC-latency bound (~2 min/run): pin fork block, reuse cache, simulate all child safes in one pass
topIssues.author: sbvegan
topIssues.body:
## Problem

Each `just simulate-stack` call takes about 2 minutes, and reviewing a stacked task needs many of them. The PR #1628 review made 8 calls:

- 084, 085 and 087 on both the `foundation` and `council` child safes,
- 086,
- the full `just simulate-stack eth`.

That took about 16 minutes, measured on 2026-11-12 with the default publicnode RPC. Each run took 108–125 s. Adding more tasks to the stack barely changes this, because the U21 upgrade (eth/084) dominates and every later target re-runs it.

## Where the time goes

**About 95% of each run is spent waiting on the RPC, not compiling or executing.**

- **Network-bound.** Sampling the running `forge` process showed about 2.3 s of CPU over about 105 s of wall time, with one HTTPS connection open to `ethereum.publicnode.com` (`foundry.toml` `[rpc_endpoints] mainnet`).
- **About 800 reads, one at a time.** Foundry's per-block cache file (`~/.foundry/cache/rpc/mainnet/<block>`) shows each run fetched about 190 accounts and 600 storage slots. At about 0.13 s per request that is about 105 s, which matches the measured time.
- **The cache is never reused.** No task `.env` sets `FORK_BLOCK_NUMBER`, so `_get-fork-block-args` (`src/justfile`) forks at the latest block. Foundry writes the cache for that block, but the next run forks a newer block and fetches everything again.
  - Test: a separate 80-slot fork script pinned to one block took 14.4 s cold and 2.4 s on the second run.
- **The same state is fetched for every run.** All calls in a review fetch the same ~800 values cold: about 6,400 sequential requests to rebuild the same state 8 times. For a nested task, each child safe re-runs the whole stack.
- **Compiling is not the bottleneck.** Logs show "No files changed, compilation skipped". The optimizer is off and `via_ir` is not used.
- **Fixed overhead is about 4 s per call:** the separate `forge script … listStack` process, the welcome message and the get-safe step.
- **L2 forks also float.** Tasks that fork the L2 (e.g. `FeeVaultUpgradeTemplate`, `vm.createSelectFork(l2RpcUrls[i])`) always use the L2 head, so pinning the L1 block does not cache them. They are small (~45 KB of state).
- **Flaky runs.** With the block unpinned, publicnode's load balancer sometimes returns `block not found`.

## Recommendations (ranked by gain vs effort)

Gains below are estimates unless marked measured.

1. **Pin the fork block for review batches (no code change).**
   - Command: `export FORK_BLOCK_NUMBER=$(cast block-number --rpc-url https://ethereum.publicnode.com)` before running the batch.
   - Expected: the first run stays ~2 min, later runs at the same block about 8–12 s, so the 8-call review drops from 16 min to about 3 min.
   - Optional code change: have `_get-fork-block-args` default to rounding the head down (e.g. `latest - latest % 50`) for `simulate*` recipes, so runs within ~10 min share the cache automatically. `sign*` recipes keep using latest.
   - Caveat: results are frozen at that block, so re-pin before signing and after any on-chain execution.
2. **Warm the cache once, then run the rest in parallel.** Each warm run uses about 2–3 s of CPU, so the whole batch takes about as long as the slowest single run (~15 s).
   - Don't run cold runs in parallel against publicnode: it rate-limits (429) and returns `block not found`.
   - Concurrent runs overwrite the same cache file. The last write wins, which is harmless.
3. **Simulate every child safe in one process** (about 50 lines, `src/tasks/StackedSimulator.sol` `_simulateStack`).
   - For each nested task: take a snapshot (`vm.snapshotState`), `executeTask` once per owner safe of the root safe, revert between them, then run once with no child safe to advance.
   - This prints hashes for every task and child safe in one run: 8 processes become 1, about 2 min cold or about 8 s warm.
4. **Faster or local RPC.**
   - `OVERRIDE_RPC_URL` already works (`src/script/get-rpc-url.sh`). Cold time scales with latency: an RPC at ~30 ms is about 4–5x faster, and a local node at ~1 ms makes cold runs as fast as warm ones. It also removes the publicnode flakes.
   - Alternative: one shared `anvil --fork-url $RPC --fork-block-number $B`, with every run pointed at `OVERRIDE_RPC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8545`. All runs share one in-memory fork, so there is no cache-file race.
5. **Pre-warm the cache for a new block (advanced, fragile).** Take the account and slot list from the previous cache file, batch-fetch it at the new block, and write the new cache file. Cold runs at a fresh block drop from ~110 s to ~10 s, but this depends on Foundry's internal cache format.
6. **Cut the fixed overhead.** Drop the separate `listStack` process, since the simulation already prints the stack. Warm runs go from ~8–10 s to ~4–5 s.

**Not worth it:** compiler settings and print-suppression flags. `FETCH_TASKS_ONLY` skips the preceding tasks, which breaks Safe nonces and therefore the hashes whenever tasks share a Safe.

## Realistic totals for the 8-call review

| Approach | Time | Speedup |
|---|---|---|
| Today (measured) | ~16 min | 1x |
| Pinned block (#1) | ~3 min | ~5x |
| Pinned + warm cache + parallel (#1 + #2) | ~15 s | ~60x |
| All child safes in one process (#3), warm cache or local node (#1/#4/#5), less overhead (#6) | ~5–8 s | ~120–200x |

Getting much below that needs a long-running simulator process: forge startup and loading artifacts take ~1–2 s, plus ~1 s of CPU to execute the stack.

## Suggested first steps

- Document the `FORK_BLOCK_NUMBER` + warm-cache workflow for reviewers (#1, #2). This needs no code change.
- Implement simulating all child safes in one pass in `StackedSimulator` (#3).
- Default `simulate*` to a rounded-down block (#1, optional part).

topPRs.title: feat(template): add OPCMUpgradeV1000 and OPCMMigrateV1000 for U22 with ZK_DISPUTE_GAME
topPRs.author: wwared
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Closes #1475. Adds templates that run the U22 (op-contracts/v10.0.0) OPCM flow, including enabling `ZK_DISPUTE_GAME` (game type 10). v10 is the first release where a production OPCM may enable ZK: optimism#23868 removed the dev-feature gate.

U22 uses three OPCM calls. Two new templates cover them:

| U22 call | Template | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 1. `upgrade()` | `OPCMUpgradeV1000` | v9 → v10. Keeps the current games and respected type (typically SPDG + SCK, respecting 9). |
| 2. `migrate()` | `OPCMMigrateV1000` | Forms the interop dependency set: shared DGF/ASR/ETHLockbox/DelayedWETH, INTEROP on. Registers SPDG + SCK with the same respected type. |
| 3. `upgrade()` (re-run) | `OPCMUpgradeV1000` | Rewrites the shared DGF/ASR: enables ZK, disables SCK, respects ZK. Later re-runs serve as the SPDG fallback (respect 5, ZK still registered). |

Why this order: v10 `migrate()` only accepts respected type 5 or 9. Its migration validator also requires SCK (`MIG-DGF-20`). So ZK can only be turned on after migration.

`OPCMUpgradeV900` is untouched; it backs the pending mainnet U21 task `eth/084`.

### `OPCMUpgradeV1000` (new; based on `OPCMUpgradeV900`)

- **v10 deltas**
  - Drops the `PermittedProxyDeployment=ETHLockbox` instruction, which v10 rejects. The template requires every chain to already have a lockbox with `ETH_LOCKBOX` enabled.
  - Adds `zkPrestate` to `ValidationInputDev` (StandardValidator 6.0.0).
  - Pins the OPCM to `10.0.0`.
  - Reads the expected DelayedWETH version from the validator's `delayedWETHImpl` instead of hard-coding it.
- **Per-chain config**
  - Explicit `superCannonKonaEnabled` / `zkEnabled` flags with their fields: SCK prestate and bond; ZK prestate (SP1 vkey), `zkMaxChallengeDuration`, `zkMaxProveDuration`, `zkChallengerBond`, `zkInitBond`.
  - A disabled game's fields must be zero.
  - The ZK bounds mirror the OPCM's `_isValidZKDisputeGameConfig`.
  - `startingRespectedGameType` must be an enabled game.
- **Task 1 keeps games:** on a chain that is not migrated, the respected type must equal the live one, the SCK registration must match `superCannonKonaEnabled`, and no ZK game may be registered. These are V900's rules. Only a migrated chain's re-run (task 3, fallback) may rotate them.
- **INTEROP gate**
  - The template refuses `zkEnabled` unless the chain has `INTEROP`: `"OPCMUpgradeV1000: ZK_DISPUTE_GAME can only be enabled on a migrated interop chain"`. This also gates respecting ZK.
  - Without it, a chain could enable ZK before `migrate()` and abandon those games on the pre-migration factory.
- **Shared-factory guard:** chains that share a DGF (a migrated set) must carry identical game configs. Otherwise each member's `upgrade()` rewrites the shared DGF/ASR and the last one silently wins. A task should list every member of the set. An unlisted member's shared contracts are still rewritten, but its chain is not validated.
- **Carry-forward:** like V900's SCK bond pin, a live game's bond, ZK durations and challenger bond must equal the config. Only prestates may change; use `SetDisputeGameArgs` (type 10 support in #1597) to change the rest.
- **Prestates:** both are checked against the pinned registry, SCK as `cannon64-kona-interop` and ZK as `kona-sp1`.
- **Post-upgrade validation**
  - Registrations and bonds match the config.
  - The ZK `gameArgs` are pinned byte-for-byte: prestate, `sp1PlonkAdapterImpl`, durations, challenger bond, ASR, WETH. The StandardValidator only bounds-checks durations and challenger bond (optimism#23872).
  - The proof-maturity delay, finality delay and DelayedWETH delay are unchanged.
  - The anchor root and anchor game are carried forward.
  - The lockbox is kept.

### `OPCMMigrateV1000` (new; port of `OPCMMigrateV900` from #1582)

v10's `MigrateInput` and `MigrationValidationInput` ABIs are byte-identical to v9's. Only these change:
- `V900` → `V1000` renames;
- a major-version gate `startsWith("10.")`;
- `zkPrestate: bytes32(0)` in the per-chain `ValidationInputDev`, since `migrate()` never registers ZK.

If #1582 changes before this lands, this port follows it.

## Verification

There is no v10 OPCM on Sepolia yet, so the full flow ran on an anvil fork of Sepolia (block 12121621) against an OPCM bootstrapped with `op-deployer bootstrap implementations` from `op-contracts/v10.0.0-rc.1`:
- `version()` returns `10.0.0`;
- `devFeatureBitmap()` returns 0;
- StandardValidator is 6.0.0.

The chains were OP Sepolia (11155420) and Unichain Sepolia (1301), both on 9.0.3 and respecting SCK. A throwaway test (not committed) drove the real templates through `simulate()`, the same nested Safe path that signers use. Every `simulate` also ran the template's own `_validate`, including the StandardValidator, and, for migrate, `validateMigratedChain`.

| Step | Config | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Task 1: `OPCMUpgradeV1000` | rgt 9, SCK on, ZK off | Both chains on `10.0.0`, still respecting 9, SCK registered, no ZK, separate DGFs. 31 slot changes across 17 contracts, no ETH moved. |
| ZK before migrate | rgt 10, ZK on | Setup reverts: `ZK_DISPUTE_GAME can only be enabled on a migrated interop chain`. |
| Task 2: `OPCMMigrateV1000` | SPDG + SCK, rgt 9 | One shared DGF, ASR and ETHLockbox. INTEROP is on for both chains. The shared ASR respects 9. Both lockboxes' ETH moves into the new shared lockbox. |
| Mismatched set configs | the two ZK bonds differ | Setup reverts: `chains sharing a DisputeGameFactory must use identical game configs`. |
| Task 3: `OPCMUpgradeV1000` | rgt 10, SCK off, ZK on | Shared ASR respects 10; the SCK impl, args and bond are cleared. ZK has impl `zkDisputeGameImpl` and bond 0.08 ETH. Its `gameArgs` are `(0x007a57c6…286c kona-sp1, sp1PlonkAdapter, 604800, 259200, 1 ETH, sharedASR, sharedWETH)`. This step changed 16 slots: the Safe nonce, the shared ASR respected type (retirement timestamp untouched) and 14 shared DGF slots. |
| ZK bond change | `zkInitBond` 0.09 ETH | Setup reverts: `zkInitBond must equal the chain's current ZK_DISPUTE_GAME bond`. |
| SPDG fallback | rgt 5, ZK still on | Shared ASR respects 5 and ZK stays registered. Two slots change: the Safe nonce and the ASR respected type. |
| Respect ZK while disabled | rgt 10, ZK off | Setup reverts: `startingRespectedGameType must be an enabled super game type (5, 9 or 10)`. |
| Rotate before migrate | rgt 5, SCK on | Setup reverts: `a chain that is not migrated must keep its respected game type`. |
| Drop SCK before migrate | live rgt rotated to 5; config rgt 5, SCK off | Setup reverts: `a chain that is not migrated must keep its SUPER_CANNON_KONA registration`. |

Every `simulate` reported StandardValidator output `""`. Migrate also reported an empty `validateMigratedChain`.

`FOUNDRY_PROFILE=ci forge build`, `forge fmt --check` and `src/script/check-struct-order.sh` pass.

## Additional context

- **Draft until the U22 rc OPCM is on Sepolia.** Example tasks, `Regression.t.sol` cases and setup tests land then. Until that happens, `template_regression_tests` (`simulate-all-templates`) flags both templates for missing an example task.
- If the release OPCM ships a version other than `10.0.0` (develop is already `10.0.1`), the single pin in `OPCMUpgradeV1000._loadOPCM` is updated in that follow-up.
- Open for interop reviewers: the exact step sequencing and who owns the full U22 task.
- **Needs a governance input before any ZK task:**
  - Nothing in the stack (template, OPCM or StandardValidator) bounds `zkMaxChallengeDuration`, `zkMaxProveDuration`, `zkChallengerBond` or `zkInitBond` beyond non-zero and ≤ `uint32` max.
  - A unit slip, such as a 600-second challenge window, would pass every check. After that, the carry-forward rule freezes the value for later re-runs.
  - The first ZK task must justify its values. If the values get a spec, the template can enforce floors and ceilings.
  - Production `zkPrestate`: the pinned registry's only `kona-sp1` entry is version `0.0.1` (`0x007a57c6…286c`). It was used here as a placeholder.

topPRs.body:

Ink Sepolia and Soneium Minato are upgraded by 115 and never migrated.

| Task | Template | Chains | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sep/125-U21-op-uni-opcm-migrate-v900` | `OPCMMigrateV900` | Unichain Sepolia (1301), OP Sepolia (11155420) | `DEPENDS_ON` 115; ascending chain-ID order, so Unichain's ProxyAdmin administers the shared proxies |

**Inputs (read on-chain 3 Nov, both chains at v8: SystemConfig 4.0.0, `lastUsedOPCMVersion` 8.0.1, respected game 9, own lockbox each):**
- Proposer: OP Sepolia's OPE proposer `0x9884…35f5` (sep/113, `DisputeGameFactory.gameArgs(5)`). Unichain Sepolia's op-proposer `0x97e7…0800` must be stopped or repointed after migration, and OP Sepolia's proposer configured for the interop set.
- Super root `0x382d95f5…9a08` @ 1793742186 from `op-chain-ops/cmd/check-super-root` over `sepolia.unichain.org` + `sepolia.optimism.io` at the latest common finalized timestamp; **refresh before signing** and regenerate hashes.
- Prestate `0x03b985…faf59` (kona-client/v1.9.0 interop, same as 115), game type 9, 0.08 ETH bond, OPCM `0x160f…39cc` (v9.0.0-rc.1, 9.0.3; swap if the final release redeploys it).
- Nonces pinned one above 115's (L1PAO 60 / FUS 83 / SC 74). sep/116 and sep/118 pin the same safes.

**Checks:** `just simulate-stack sep 125-U21-op-uni-opcm-migrate-v900 council` on top of 115 passed on 3 Nov (Sepolia block ~12058200) with empty validator output for both chains; `VALIDATION.md` has both child-safe hashes, the root Safe tx hash and the full calldata. State-change section is descriptive; per-slot Tenderly review still to do before READY TO SIGN. sep/121 (the same call on Jacob's devnet pair) cost 17.0M gas on Sepolia, so `TENDERLY_GAS` is 30M.

Open before un-drafting: final v9.0.0 OPCM address, the super root refresh, Tenderly slot review, Security review of the template PRs, and confirmation that OP + Unichain is the whole Sepolia interop set (the migrate scope is not written in the records yet).

topPRs.title: feat(template): add OPCMMigrateV900
topPRs.author: 0xOneTony
topPRs.body:
Adds `OPCMMigrateV900`, a template that calls `OPContractsManagerV2.migrate` to move a set of chains onto a shared `ETHLockbox`, `DisputeGameFactory` and `AnchorStateRegistry` in one delegatecall from the ProxyAdmin owner, then checks the result with `StandardValidator.validateMigratedChain`. It registers `SUPER_PERMISSIONED` and `SUPER_CANNON_KONA` on the shared factory, requires `l2chains` in ascending chain ID order, and takes the shared addresses for validation from the contracts the migration creates, since their CREATE2 salt includes `block.timestamp`.

The example task `sep/044-opcm-migrate-v900` uses placeholder values and is skipped in `simulate-all-templates` until a v9 OPCM exists and the chains are upgraded to it.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/1573

topPRs.title: sep/900-902: Whitechain Sepolia U19, U20 and U21 tasks
topPRs.author: donoso-eth
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds the Upgrade 19, 20 and 21 tasks for **Whitechain Sepolia (chain id 1874)**.

Whitechain is permissioned-only, runs **custom gas token v2**, has its own SuperchainConfig and is
**not in the superchain-registry**, so all three tasks read addresses from a local `addresses.json` via `fallbackAddressesJsonPath`.

**Draft deliberately.** Only `sep/900` is signable today; 901 and 902 are blocked drafts with stub validation files, since each upgrade gates on the previous one. This is being shared with the Whitechain team first, so please do not review for approval yet.

| Task | Upgrade | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `sep/900-U19-whitechain-testnet` | v6.0.0 → v7.0.0, OPCM 7.1.17 | **Ready to sign**, simulated clean, hash confirmed at Safe nonce 4 |
| `sep/901-U20-whitechain-testnet` | v7.0.0 → v8.0.0, OPCM 8.0.1 | Draft, blocked |
| `sep/902-U21-whitechain-testnet` | v8.0.0 → v9.0.0, OPCM 9.0.3 | Draft, blocked |

## Rehearsed before being written

The whole sequence was rehearsed on a replica devnet (chain id 18740) that mirrors 1874 on every structural property. There, **U19, the Karst L2 fork, U20 and U21 were all executed**, and each upgrade's post-execution state matched its predicted diff, including the U19 DelayedWETH proxy and the U21 ETHLockbox both landing at the addresses their simulations predicted. The replica tasks are not in this PR; they existed only during the rehearsal.

topPRs.title: feat(template): add OPCMUpgradeV900
topPRs.author: ZakAyesh
topPRs.body:
Adds `OPCMUpgradeV900`, the upgrade half of the v9 (interop) release: it calls `OPContractsManagerV2.upgradeSuperchain` once, then `upgrade` per chain, so a set of chains already on op-contracts/v8 steps onto the v9 OPCM.

**Ordering:** this task runs before the `OPCMMigrateV900` task in #1582. `migrate` requires every chain to already be on the v9 OPCM.

Differences from `OPCMUpgradeV800`, all driven by the v9 OPCM:
- The only permitted upgrade instruction is `overrides.cfg.startingRespectedGameType`; the `startingAnchorRoot` override is rejected, so the anchor-root inputs are gone and the super-root anchor is carried forward. `_validate` asserts the respected game type landed and the anchor was not cleared.
- Version gate accepts any 9.x and checks `isPermittedUpgradeSequence` per chain.
- SUPER_CANNON_KONA is enabled when the factory already carries it (v8 cleared the CANNON_KONA impl it used to key off).
- `Challenger` is read with a tolerant lookup: super-game-only chains register none.

**Example task and simulation.** `sep/045-opcm-upgrade-v900` (Unichain Sepolia + OP Sepolia) simulates against the throwaway v9 OPCM (9.0.5) Andrea deployed on Sepolia on 2026-10-22 for template testing (`0xe09c417496c786abffefa676da9e11aab2c32ea9`, not an rc, no tag, no registry entry). The simulation passes end to end at fork block 11999987 with no validator errors for either chain. A real task must point at the released v9 OPCM. The example is not skipped in `simulate-all-templates`, so CI depends on that throwaway contract staying deployed; happy to add a skip like #1582 if preferred.

Setup tests: `test/template/OPCMUpgradeV900Setup.t.sol` (5 tests, Sepolia fork).

Open for review: the prestate in the example is the chains' current SUPER_CANNON_KONA prestate as a placeholder, and the ZK game path is unsupported as in V800.
